editor_note: The German is faithful and reads naturally. Terms are correct and used consistently: "low-overhead quantum error detection" becomes "ressourcenschonende Quantenfehlererkennung", error mitigation becomes "Fehlerminderung", and PNA's "absorbing the inverses of the learned noise channels into observables" becomes "Inversen der erlernten Rauschkanäle … in Observablen absorbiert". The informal "du" holds throughout ("erfährst du").

All three rewritten entries match the English: "Brich in Pipelines und Notebooks frühzeitig ab" is an idiomatic rendering of "fail fast", "Rufe ein einzelnes Backend ab" fits `backend()`, and entry 68 keeps "Circuit Function" and "KI-gestützte Quantenkontrolltechniken" consistent with the rest of the page.

The meaning is faithful throughout this short changelog, and nothing would mislead a learner. There is one stiff spot. Entry [5] copies the English word order: the purpose phrase comes after the comma ("wurde veröffentlicht, zur Migration von `qiskit-ibm-runtime`-Code"). A native writer would put it before the verb instead. The terms are fine and consistent: "Qiskit-Skills", "Änderungsprotokoll", "Skill-Releases".

examples.source: The `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime` skill was released, for migrating `qiskit-ibm-runtime` code.
examples.translation: Der Skill `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime` wurde veröffentlicht, zur Migration von `qiskit-ibm-runtime`-Code.
examples.suggested: Der Skill `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime` zur Migration von `qiskit-ibm-runtime`-Code wurde veröffentlicht.
examples.why: The purpose phrase after the comma copies the English word order and reads awkwardly in German. Putting it before the verb is the natural phrasing.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The hedge in "might be faster" is kept as "schneller sein ... können", and the informal du register holds ("Sieh dir ... an", "findest du"). The one change an editor would make is in entry [9]: "Qiskit patterns" is IBM's name for its workflow framework, so it should not be translated literally as "Qiskit-Muster". Keep the name, as in "Qiskit Patterns und Workflows".

examples.source: seamlessly integrate the service into their current Qiskit patterns and workflows
examples.translation: nahtlos in ihre bestehenden Qiskit-Muster und -Workflows zu integrieren
examples.suggested: nahtlos in ihre bestehenden Qiskit Patterns und Workflows zu integrieren
examples.why: "Qiskit patterns" is the name of IBM's workflow framework. A literal "Muster" hides that it is a proper name, so the learner can't link it to the Qiskit Patterns docs. The meaning is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: Entry 9 matches the English and reads naturally: "Rust-gestützte Performance-Verbesserungen", "Auswahl des Hardware-Layouts für Schaltkreise" and "reduzieren den Kompilierungs-Overhead und verbessern die Fidelity" keep every claim, and it uses the same terms as the rest of the page.

None of the 8 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The caveats, quantities and conditions all carry over: the On-Prem exception in [162], "75-fache Beschleunigung" and the list of incompatibilities in [272], and "als experimentelle Option" in [289]. The main problem is terminology. The rewritten entries render "circuit" two ways: [162] uses "dynamischen Schaltkreise", which matches the rest of the page ([11], [21], [163], [165], [200]), but [261], [263] and [272] switch to "dynamische Circuits" and "Circuit-Dauer". There are also two stiff phrasings: "innerhalb des Bodys eines Zweigs" in [269] is an awkward anglicism, and "die sie im Utility-Maßstab ermöglichen" in [261] is a calque.

examples.source: new features to [dynamic circuits](...) that will enable them at the utility scale
examples.translation: neue Funktionen für [dynamische Circuits](...) einführen, die sie im Utility-Maßstab ermöglichen
examples.suggested: neue Funktionen für [dynamische Schaltkreise](...) einführen, die ihren Einsatz im Utility-Maßstab ermöglichen
examples.why: The rest of the page, including the rewritten [162] and the parallel entry [163], uses 'Schaltkreise', so 'Circuits' here is inconsistent. Also, 'die sie ... ermöglichen' is a calque of 'enable them'.
The near-identical entry [165] already says 'Schaltkreisdauer'. The same item should use the same term.

examples.source: inside the body of a branch (as in, nested control flow)
examples.suggested: innerhalb des Rumpfs eines Zweigs (also verschachtelter Kontrollfluss)
examples.why: 'des Bodys' is an anglicism with an awkward genitive. German technical writing says 'Rumpf', or simply 'innerhalb eines Zweigs'.
